Messages.Author: Sigmund Bjornstein
Messages.Body:
Greetings, everyone.

I find myself doubting a ruling made against me in a tournament,
yesterday. I tried to play Golconda on my _own_ Anson, and was told
that Golconda cannot be played on my own vampires... only on another
methuselah's vampires. This was a big reversal for me at this point (I
was rather counting on that Golconda for me).

Is this true? Because I can't find it anywhere. The text for
"Golconda: Inner Peace" says "Play on a vampire with a capacity above
7". Not a word about "controlled by another methuselah", for example.
Is there some errata that I have missed?

Thanks, and regards,

Sigmund Bjornstein

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>I find myself doubting a ruling made against me in a tournament,
>yesterday. I tried to play Golconda on my _own_ Anson, and was told
>that Golconda cannot be played on my own vampires... only on another
>methuselah's vampires. This was a big reversal for me at this point (I
>was rather counting on that Golconda for me).

You were right. Card text:

Golconda: Inner Peace [Jyhad, V:TES]
Cardtype: Master
Master.
Only usable on a vampire with a capacity above 7. {Remove the vampire from the
game}. His or her controller gains pool equal to the vampire's capacity. The
controller may cancel this card by burning 2 pool.

Whoever tried to convince you otherwise was either very ignorant or very
sneaky! Golconda often is used to cause a 2 pool loss for your predator/prey
(if they don't want to waste time losing their big vamp) so maybe he thought it
could only be used for that. Also, Golconda is often used for decks that rely
on a single, big vampire. If the vampire gets low on blood or is stuck in
torpor, Golconda prevents the self-contesting problem.

So to reiterate, Golconda can indeed be used on your own vampires.

Halcyan 2
